module_title: Panchayati Raj - Committees, Key Articles, and Reservations
introduction: At this level, we study the evolution of PRIs through various committees, specific constitutional articles (from 243 to 243O), and the strict reservation policies for women and marginalized communities.

core_concepts.title: Evolutionary Committees
core_concepts.description: 1. Ashok Mehta (1977): Recommended a '2-tier' system. 2. GVK Rao (1985): Emphasized the Zila Parishad. 3. LM Singhvi (1986): First committee to strongly recommend granting 'Constitutional Status' to PRIs.

core_concepts.title: Gram Sabha (Article 243A)
core_concepts.description: It is the primary body of the Panchayati Raj system. It consists of ALL registered voters residing within the area of a Gram Panchayat. It is a permanent body and the foundation of the system.

core_concepts.title: Reservation of Seats (Article 243D)
core_concepts.description: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to their population. Crucially, not less than 1/3rd (33%) of the total seats and chairperson positions at all levels MUST be reserved for women. (Some states like Bihar and MP have increased this to 50%).

core_concepts.title: State Election Commission (Article 243K)
core_concepts.description: The superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all panchayat elections are vested in the State Election Commission. The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.

core_concepts.title: State Finance Commission (Article 243-I)
core_concepts.description: The Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every 5 years to review the financial position of the panchayats and recommend the distribution of taxes between the state and the panchayats.

important_entities.name: 11th Schedule
important_entities.significance: Added by the 73rd Amendment, it lists 29 matters (like agriculture, rural roads, drinking water) over which the panchayats have jurisdiction and responsibility.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common trap! The 'Election Commission of India' (ECI) does NOT conduct panchayat or municipality elections. This is the exclusive domain of the 'State Election Commission' (SEC).
States having a population of less than 20 lakhs are EXEMPTED from constituting the intermediate level (Panchayat Samiti). They can have a 2-tier system (Village and District).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: I for Income, K for Konducting elections
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Article 243-I = Finance Commission (Income). Article 243-K = Election Commission.

exam_strategy_tips: Match the Following questions frequently pair the Committee names with their key recommendations (e.g., Ashok Mehta -> 2-tier, LM Singhvi -> Constitutional Status).
Remember that the reservation of 1/3rd seats for women is a mandatory provision, not optional.
